# Events Flow Up

#### Course: Build your First Web App with React

## Events Flow Up

We could now move on to handling the submit function, but I want you to understand a simple yet important concept first.

You already know data flows down (the parent passes props to its children). But this isn't true for events; after all, they flow up from the child to the parent.

It's quite simple, really. The child runs a function (provided by its parent) that can update the parent's state.

So, the parent "listens" for the event, and the child "notifies" it by calling the function. Hence, the execution happens in the child, with its result going "upward" to its parent.

Let's apply this concept to our code!

- App will pass an onAddEntry callback to JournalForm.
- When the user submits their entry, JournalForm will call onAddEntry(title, content).
- As a result, the callback will add the new entry to the list inside our App.

![Events Flow Up](data:image/png;base64,)

With this nuance out of the way, let's focus on handling the form submission.
